Líikʼs has clear raise/lift semantics; related liʼis/líikʼes forms also have put-away/store uses, so it must not be rejected merely because a lifting sense exists. I cannot confidently establish that this exact lexeme/form naturally communicates preserving a digital file or edits here. Hold these TEN save-dependent P0 keys for a focused lexical decision, not an exact-published-sentence gate. In the question, a kʼáat a ...-ik is desire plus dependent action; in failure, maʼ béeychaj expresses past inability, not prohibition. Those grammatical merits do not resolve the storage verb.
